cells.value: What a partner needs to get the code: the four private repos the rebuild runs on, what each holds, and how to get access and clone them. Students don't get these repos: they get the student edition, a generated copy of the workbook and the code with every client shown as a label, no git history and no keys (Rebuild from zero, step 0.5; play spp-p32a, notes/student-edition.md). It closes gap G02 of the second replication check (spp-c4): the steps ran code that lives only in private repos. Facts from play spp-p20a (notes/gap-facts-g02.md, notes/gap-facts.md). 2. How a partner gets access and clones (students get the student edition instead)
Alex (or his agent, with a normal git push)
Push agents-home and master-connector-repo so GitHub holds the commit this tab names. On 2026-10-01 Alex's Mac was 31 and 10 commits ahead of GitHub; a newcomer clones only what GitHub has.
On Alex's Mac, after git fetch, git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD prints 0 in ~/.agents and in ~/Projects/master-connector-repo.
Sign up at github.com if you don't have an account, then send your GitHub username to Alex (alex@increaseroas.com).
You can sign in at github.com and see your username on your profile.

agents-home and master-connector-repo are in the increase-roas organization since 2026-10-02, so each person gets a role per repo there: Read (pull only) or Write (pull and push). Alex chose Read for the partner invited on 2026-10-02. On the two repos still owned by Alex's personal account (ghl-command-universal and increase-roas-oauth-gateway) every collaborator can read AND push: a personal account's private repo has only owner and collaborator levels. Read-only there needs the same move, or a read-only deploy key per repo and machine (it never expires and isn't tied to a person).

Each person's role on each repo is written down before step 3 (Read unless they must push). The partner of 2026-10-02: Read on agents-home, master-connector-repo and the Director's home; nothing on the two Worker repos.

For each repo the person needs: open https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> (owner increase-roas for agents-home and master-connector-repo, increaseroasir for the two Worker repos), then Settings > Access > Collaborators (in the organization: Collaborators and teams) > Add people. Type the username, pick the match, choose the role in the organization (Read unless they must push), and add them. Invite by username: a pending invitation sent by email takes an organization seat. Script route: PUT /repos/<owner>/<repo>/collaborators/<username>, which also sends the invite; a pending invitation's role changes with PATCH /repos/<owner>/<repo>/invitations/<id> (permissions=read, as on 2026-10-02). GitHub allows 50 invitations per repo per 24 hours. Most newcomers need agents-home and master-connector-repo; the two Worker repos are only for rebuilding the GHL routes.
The person shows as a pending invite on the repo's access page, and GET /repos/<owner>/<repo>/invitations lists the open invitation with its role (read for the 2026-10-02 partner).

Accept each repo's invitation (there is one per repo) from the email GitHub sends or the notifications page on github.com. By API: GET /user/repository_invitations, then PATCH /user/repository_invitations/<invitation id>.

https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> (increase-roas for agents-home and master-connector-repo, increaseroasir for the Worker repos) opens while you are signed in, instead of a not-found page, and the repo's access page lists you.
5. Sign the Mac in to GitHub
Sign in once with gh auth login (Rebuild step 2.2) as the account Alex invited. A private repo clones only for a signed-in account that has access.
The clones in steps 6 to 9 finish without a permission error.

git clone https://github.com/increase-roas/agents-home.git ~/.agents && bash ~/.agents/tools/unify/git_setup.sh. The setup script links the tracked post-commit hook into .git/hooks, runs the secret scan and keeps the committed .gitignore. Until Phase 8 points the scripts at your own hub, the hook's notes sync still targets Alex's hub.

git -C ~/.agents log -1 --format=%h prints the commit in section 1. skills/, instructions/, tools/cards/, tools/connectors/ and tools/unify/ exist. .git/hooks/post-commit links to tools/unify/hooks/post-commit, and the scan reports 0 hits.

git clone https://github.com/increase-roas/master-connector-repo.git ~/Projects/master-connector-repo. Use exactly this path: the agents-home hook rewrites the workbook there and also writes a copy to ~/Documents. Nothing to install. Read AGENTS.md, then STATUS.md. Student route: the edition's master-connector-repo already holds the workbook at work/2026-09-30_composio-connect/connectors-2026-09-30.xlsx (the same bytes as connectors-student-edition.xlsx, at the path the agents-home hook writes) and a blank STATUS.md (the repo-conform skeleton), so this step's check passes on the student copy too.
work/2026-09-30_composio-connect/connectors-2026-09-30.xlsx exists in the clone, and git log -1 --format=%h prints the commit in section 1.

8. Clone the GHL builder (only to rebuild it)

git clone https://github.com/increaseroasir/ghl-command-universal.git ~/Development/ghl-command-universal. Then, in worker/: npm ci, npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run build, which builds dist/index.js with the pinned wrangler 4.143.0. The origin/ half goes onto the hub: copy server.py and test_origin.py to /opt/ghl-command-universal, run npm ci there, and install the two supervisor programs from origin/deploy/supervisor/. Its secrets (origin key, tunnel token, GHL Command sign-in) are not in git (gap G14).
Tests and typecheck pass and worker/dist/index.js exists. On the hub, python3 /opt/ghl-command-universal/test_origin.py passes.
